To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the radion contribution to $s_{\rm w}$ can be sizable if the radion mass is around TeV, and that the radion can induce a sizable contribution to $g-2_\mu$ and $K_L-K_0$.
the radion can induce a sizable contribution to the weak-mixing angle if the vacuum-expectation value and the mass are around TeV.
the radion in Randall-Sundrum compactification can induce a sizable contribution to the weak angle, if the mass is around TeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phenomenological aspects of the Randall-Sundum compactification, and the possible implications of this model to the physics beyond the Standard Model.
the effects of the radion in the weak mixing angle, the $K_L$-$K_S$ mass difference, and the $(g-2)_{\mu}$.
the effects of the radion in the RS model on the electroweak parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if the RS compactification is realized in Nature, the weak mixing angle and the $K_L$-$K_S$ mass difference are good probes to the TeV scale radion physics.
the radion contribution to $sin^2\theta_W$ is not ruled out by any existing data.
a radion with a mass of about a TeV is excluded by the current precision data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RS model is consistent with all the precision data if the mass of the lightest Kaluza-Klein (KK) mode of the graviton is above a few TeV.
the RS model can be ruled out if the weak mixing angle is measured to be $s^2_W=0.2313\pm 0.0004$, and the bound can be relaxed if the measurement is not so precise.
the radion contribution to $\sin^2\theta_W$ is comparable with the one from the top quark.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radion is a viable candidate to explain the discrepancy between the measured value of the weak mixing angle and the prediction of the Standard Model.
the RS model is a viable candidate for physics beyond the SM.
, if the RS model is realized in Nature, we can expect that the weak mixing angle is modified from its standard value, and the modification may be observed in the future experiments.
